title: Monitor how real users experience your app

blocks.content: Set up two views of your website: Synthetic Monitoring checks availability from outside your network, and Frontend Observability collects real user performance and errors from the browser.

blocks.prompt: Enter your website origin, such as https://yourcompany.com. Both setups use it.

blocks.content: First, point an uptime check at {{appUrl}}. You need permission to create checks.
Open **Synthetic Monitoring**.
blocks.tooltip: Open the setup page in this Grafana instance.

blocks.content: If prompted, click **Get started**. If you cannot initialize the service, ask an administrator, then return here; skip this step only when setup is already complete.
blocks.tooltip: This one-time setup must finish before you can create a check.

blocks.content: Click **Create new check** once setup is complete.
blocks.tooltip: If this is unavailable, finish service setup with an administrator first.

blocks.content: Open **API Endpoint** and keep the default **HTTP** request type and **GET** method.
blocks.tooltip: Open the setup page in this Grafana instance.

blocks.content: Enter a descriptive **Job name**, such as `my-website-uptime`.

steps.formHint: Enter a descriptive name for your application or check.
steps.tooltip: This name becomes the job label used to find the check in metrics and logs.
steps.description: Enter a descriptive **Job name**, such as `my-website-uptime`.

blocks.content: Set **Request target** to {{appUrl}}.
blocks.tooltip: An HTTP check requests this URL; it does not execute JavaScript or simulate a complete browser session.

blocks.content: Click **Execution** to choose probe locations and a schedule.
blocks.tooltip: Each selected location runs the check independently at the frequency you choose.

blocks.content: Select the highlighted online probe, or keep it selected. Leave **Frequency** at its default and review the estimated usage before saving.

steps.reftarget: label:has(+ :is(label, div) [data-testid='probes cards status'][aria-label$=' is online']) input[data-testid='checkEditor form probeCheckbox']:not(:disabled):nth-match(1)
steps.tooltip: Start with one online location; each additional probe increases usage.

steps.reftarget: label:has(+ :is(label, div) [data-testid='probes cards status'][aria-label$=' is online']) input[data-testid='checkEditor form probeCheckbox']:not(:disabled):checked:nth-match(1)
steps.description: Confirm an online probe is selected.
steps.tooltip: Continue once an online location is selected.

blocks.reftarget: form[data-testid='checkEditor form']:has(label:has(input[data-testid='checkEditor form probeCheckbox']:checked) + :is(label, div):has([data-testid='probes cards status'][aria-label$=' is online'])) button[data-testid='checkEditor form submit']:not(:disabled)
blocks.content: Click **Save**. If an error appears, correct it and try again before continuing.
blocks.tooltip: Review the target, selected probes, and estimated usage before saving.

blocks.content: Confirm that the saved check’s dashboard opens. **Uptime** shows when at least one probe succeeds; the first results can take a few minutes.
blocks.tooltip: An empty chart immediately after saving does not mean the check failed.

blocks.content: The saved HTTP check will test {{appUrl}} from the selected location.
Next, create a Frontend Observability application for the same origin; you need permission to create applications.
Open **Connect your web application** in **Frontend Observability**.
blocks.tooltip: Open the setup page in this Grafana instance.

blocks.content: Enter your own **Application name**, such as `my-web-app`.

steps.formHint: Enter a descriptive name for your application or check.
steps.tooltip: Use a name that distinguishes this frontend from other applications and environments.
steps.description: Enter your own **Application name**, such as `my-web-app`.

blocks.content: Set **Allowed origins** to {{appUrl}}.
blocks.tooltip: Use the scheme, hostname, and port your visitors use; add other environments separately.

blocks.content: Click **Next**. If creation fails, correct the error and try again.
blocks.tooltip: Creating the application does not send browser data; you must still install and deploy Faro.

blocks.content: After the application is created, choose **Manual instrumentation**.
blocks.tooltip: These instructions appear only after the application has been created successfully.

blocks.content: Your application is created and its installation instructions are ready.
Finally, copy the Faro snippet that sends real user data from {{appUrl}}:
Keep **NPM** or **Yarn** selected, then click **Copy** once the application’s Faro initialization snippet loads. Install the SDK and add the snippet to your frontend before deploying.
blocks.tooltip: Wait for your application’s collector URL to load; if configuration loading fails, reopen its SDK instructions and retry.

blocks.content: You have the Faro snippet for this application; deploy it in your website to start sending browser telemetry.
After deploying Faro, you can compare availability checks with real user sessions and errors for {{appUrl}}. Source maps and alert rules are optional and can be configured later.
